title: X's Paid Partnerships policy: undisclosed paid partnership

jurisdiction.name: X's own rules (applies on X wherever the user is)

instrument: X Help Center, Paid Partnerships Policy
section: What are Paid Partnerships?; Rules for Paid Partnerships
binding_note: X's own terms for users of X. Policies change without notice; the retrieval date and hash record the version read.

in_force.note: The page carries no date. Recorded as read on 2026-10-22.

sources.note: help.x.com answered scripted requests with a Cloudflare challenge (403), so the page was read in a browser. The hash is over the HTML bytes the browser fetched with credentials omitted; two fetches gave the same hash. The page shows the X logo as an image where the name appears; quotes write it as [X]. 233,829 bytes. The page shows no revision date.

quotes.text: [X] defines paid partnerships as the involvement of a third-party brand providing compensation or incentives to a user, such as an influencer or content creator, to promote their product or service.

quotes.locator: Rules for Paid Partnerships, second rule
quotes.text: Posts that are part of a Paid Partnership published as an organic Post must have the “Paid Partnership” disclosure on.

elements.label: The post is part of a paid partnership: a brand gave the poster compensation or incentives to promote its product
elements.note: Shown for labelled posts, by the poster's own disclosure. For unlabelled posts a partnership is not visible.

elements.label: It was published as an organic post
The "Paid Partnership" disclosure is not on
elements.note: Daylight Commons sees unlabelled posts that share a template with labelled ones. That is consistent with a missing disclosure, and it is also what fans copying a paid post look like.

does_not_prove: A platform policy is the platform's own rule, not law. A match on visible elements is a comparison with the published policy text; only X decides whether its policy was broken, and the policy can change after the retrieval date.
